# VOLTYARD: the arena shooter template (NetNet game runtime, Template 2)

> A twin-stick arena shooter for up to 16 players, with bots filling empty
> seats. Rounds last a few minutes; the top of the board takes the round.
> You change the game by editing src/game.ts only. The template already has
> loadouts, aiming, projectiles, lag-compensated beams, death and respawn,
> heal drops, rounds, a scoreboard, bots, netcode, rendering, touch and
> gamepad controls, earn and the store. Do not write renderers, netcode,
> physics or bot AI.

## Files

- src/game.ts: THE GAME. Declarations against @netnetcapital/engine:
  game(), prefab(), weapon(), upgrade(), system(), earn.rule(), store.sku().
- src/names.json: the title and every label players read (weapons,
  upgrades, earn rules, store items).
- Everything else is template machinery.

## Rules the build enforces

- game({ template: "arena", style: "lowpoly" }) with players.loadout (1 to 4
  declared weapons), an arena { halfSize, pillars, spawns } and a round.
- Arena weapons are kind "blaster", "beam" or "nova" (never bolt or orbit).
- Asset ids look like "style.lowpoly.mini_male_f", never URLs or paths, and must be in the asset library.
- game({ style }) is the art style the creator picked: lowpoly, toon, ps1, pixel, voxel or handdrawn. Keep it. The template draws everything in it, and a "style.lowpoly.<name>" id draws as that style's own model of the same name when the style has one.
- Ids are lower_snake_case. Every game declares at least one earn.rule and one earn.stake (the buy-in run).
- Pillars fit on the floor; spawns sit 1 m inside the floor and 1 m clear of pillars.
- 4 players plus seat bots must all score kills, and an earn rule must fire,
  in a 4-minute playtest. A round should end within about 4 minutes.

## Units

Seconds, metres, metres per second, hit points (players have 100).
Tick rate 60 Hz (shooters). Yaw 0 aims up the screen (-z).

## The loop

Players spawn at a spawn point no opponent can see and at least 12 m from
all of them (a floor point when no declared spawn qualifies), with 2 s of
protection on joining, on respawn and at each new round (firing ends it). They move with one stick or WASD, aim with the
other or the mouse, hold fire, and pick weapons with 1 2 3 (or cycle).
A killed player drops players.drop (a heal cell), waits players.respawn
seconds and comes back. A round ends after round.seconds, or when someone
reaches round.frags kills; the end screen shows the board, then a new round.

## Common changes

### Tune a weapon
weapon("arc_rifle", { kind: "blaster", damage: 12, cooldown: 0.15, range: 26, speed: 44 });
blaster: count projectiles fanned over spread degrees at speed m/s for range m.
beam: an instant hit to range m (pillars stop it); the server rewinds what
the shooter saw (lag compensation), so keep cooldown at 0.8 s or more.
nova: hits every opponent within range m (a short-range blast).

### Add a weapon to the loadout
weapon("ion_cannon", { kind: "blaster", damage: 40, cooldown: 1.2, range: 30, speed: 22, pierce: 2 });
players.loadout: ["arc_rifle", "scatter_coil", "rail_lance", "ion_cannon"] (at most 4; slot 4 is reached by cycling).
Add its label to names.json weapons.

### Change the yard
arena: { halfSize: 26, pillars: [[x, z, radius], ...], spawns: [[x, z], ...] }.
Smaller halfSize and more pillars make closer fights. Keep spawns spread out.

### Change round length or the kill target
round: { seconds: 180, frags: 25 }. 120 to 300 seconds plays well.

### More or fewer bots
players.bots: 6 fills a room up to 6 players with bots (0 turns them off).
Bots never earn, and killing a bot pays no earn rule (it still scores and
shows in the kill feed). players.max caps humans in one room. Bots go easy on a
person with a poor record and sharpen as they win, ease off once they
lead the best person (they never stop shooting), and never take the round
(only a person reaches round.frags; the end screen names the best person).

### Faster respawn, bigger heals
players.respawn: 2; prefab("volt_cell", { ..., kind: "pickup", value: 50 }).

### Add an earn rule
earn.rule("first_blood", { when: "opponent.killed", n: 1, pay: 2, oncePer: "run" });
Events: opponent.killed (credits the killer), player.died (credits the one
who died), round.top (the top fragger when a round ends), round.finished
(everyone present at the end), run.won, and anything you emit(). A run is a
round. Each rule pays once per round per player, in coins; the room server
is the referee; bots never earn. Bot kills never pay: opponent.killed for a
bot's death, and anything a system emits while handling it (a streak that a
bot kill completes), score but count toward no earn rule. round.top pays
only when another person was in the round, never for topping a board of
bots. Alone with bots a player earns nothing from kills or the board.

### The buy-in run (required)
earn.stake({ min: 10, max: 100, multiple: 2 });
Every game declares one, on one top-level line; a game without it does not
build. A player stakes coins at the start of a run (the Kit spends them as
coins.spend(amount, "stake"), then the client calls conn.stake()). The room
fixes the stake when the next run starts. A staked run pays its normal earn
plus a share of stake x multiple: the share is the part of the run's most
earn the player makes. What it does not win back stays in the reward pool.
multiple is 1 to 2. "stake" is reserved: never a SKU or meta upgrade id.

### PvP pot (optional, arena only)
earn.pot({ entry: 20, recycle: 0.05 });
Each entrant pays the entry (coins.spend(entry, "pot"), then conn.pot()) and
joins the next round's pot. At the round's end the pot, less the recycle
share that stays in the reward pool, is split by the earn each entrant made.
A round where no entrant earned recycles the whole pot. "pot" is reserved.

### Losable gear (optional)
store.sku("plating_kit", { coins: 120, grants: { gear: "plating", loseBelow: 0.25 } });
Gear is owned in the player's profile and sells for coins only. It brings one
level of its declared upgrade into every staked run, and is lost when that run
makes less than loseBelow of its most earn. Its coins stay in the reward pool.

### Track something with a system
system("streaks", ({ on, emit }) => {
  const streak = new Map<number, number>();
  on("opponent.killed", (ids) => { for (const id of ids) { const n = (streak.get(id) ?? 0) + 1; streak.set(id, n); if (n === 5) emit("streak.five", [id]); } });
  on("player.died", (ids) => { for (const id of ids) streak.set(id, 0); });
});
emit(event, ids) credits those players; emit(event) credits everyone present.
players() gives each player's id, position, health, alive, kills, deaths, bot.

### Coins: earn and the store

Every game has coins: 1 coin = 1 of the game's own token, and players see
them under the token's own name, symbol and logo (never "coins" or "tokens"
as a label). Earn rules pay coins (pay is whole coins). The recommended
coin model (the default) sells in-round consumables and looks, never
permanent stat power:

store.sku("plating", { coins: 40 });                                  // one level of the "plating" upgrade for the round
store.sku("skin_neon", { coins: 300, grants: { cosmetic: 1 } });      // a finish, owned for good (saved in the player's profile)

A store item named after a declared upgrade(...) is a round upgrade: the
room grants one level of it when a player pays. Keep the five SKUs the
client is wired to (plating, servo, capacitor, skin_neon, skin_chrome) at
their prices, with the finishes' grants (neon 1, chrome 2). "Cosmetics only":
economy({ store: "cosmetics" }). Permanent upgrades are opt-in:
economy({ metaUpgrades: true }) and metaUpgrade(...), capped by the engine
at +15% a stat and +30% in all (see GAME-DESIGN.md). Price against what a round pays (the four rules here pay up
to 51): an upgrade under a round, a finish a few rounds. Before the game
launches coins are play money; the Kit switches by itself.

### Change who the players are (the asset library)
players.prefab is a real CC0 character by id; each player is drawn in their
colour holding a blaster, and plays its walk, run and shoot animations.
players: { prefab: "style.lowpoly.soldier", ... } or a dressed original:
players: { prefab: "style.lowpoly.blocky_g", appearance: { tint: "#16e0ff", parts: ["antenna"] }, ... }
appearance: { tint: "#rrggbb", accent: "#rrggbb", scale: 0.4 to 3, parts: up to 4 }.
The heal cell is prefab("volt_cell", { model: "style.lowpoly.cell_heal", ... });
any pickup model works (style.lowpoly.gem_pink, style.lowpoly.coin, style.lowpoly.burger).

## Systems API

every(seconds, n => ...), after(seconds, fn), onTick(fn), spawn(prefab, [x,y,z]),
spawnRing(prefab, { count, radius, around? }), alive(prefab?), players(),
emit(event, ids?), on(event, ids => ...), end("won" | "lost"), random(),
tick(), time(). Enemies are optional in the arena: a declared enemy prefab
spawned by a system chases the nearest player and can be shot.

## Test

engine.test.run({ ticks: 60 * 240, bots: 4, assert: [...] }) plays the game
on the server sim with 4 players plus seat bots and reports kills, deaths,
rounds (runs.won), topScore, scorers, earned by rule, softlock and ms per tick.
